Adampol – Polonezköy

Memorial of Atatürk's 1937 visit

Village musicians played a krakowiak for Atatürk – and legend has it that the President then joined the dance.

Theme
Adampol – Polonezköy
District
Beykoz
Period
1937
Visiting
Seen from outside

The story

In 1937 Mustafa Kemal Atatürk came to Adampol, and the village still talks about the day. The visit itself is certain – Turkish and Polish sources record it – but many details are known only from later retellings.

According to an account published by the newspaper Hürriyet in 2004, the villagers greeted their guest in the old Polish way, with bread and salt, and at the table Atatürk asked to see Polish dances; village musicians played a krakowiak on fiddle and accordion.

How to visit

The bust and the plaque stone are in the village centre; their exact positions are not on any map, so the pin marks the centre by the 'Polonezköy Muhtarlığı' bus stop. Look for the Turkish and Polish flags in the square. Both are outdoors and can be seen at any time.
